title: Reviewer Artifact v1
description: Structured output produced by a single reviewer role. This is the contract between reviewers and the read-only judge stage implemented by aggregate.mjs. The judge consumes ONLY these artifacts; it never reads PR comments or PR reviews. A reviewer that wants a human's inline comment to block must ingest it via `gh api` and fold it into blocking_issues[] with source: "inline_comment". See docs/ci-pipeline.md.

role.description: Adding a role here is a two-step change: reviewer artifacts are validated against main's copy of this schema, so the new value must be merged to main before a PR can emit it.

decision_ref.description: The design-doc decision or finding this blocker cites, e.g. "D6" or "RA-014". The invariant reviewer is expected to populate this: a blocker that cannot name the contract it violates is usually an opinion.

source.description: How this blocker was discovered. `inline_comment` means the reviewer ingested a human's inline PR comment.

confidence.description: Optional. The fourth instance of the class `id`, `decision_ref`, `severity` and `source` were admitted to close, and the one most certain to recur: `confidence` is *required* on every fix_suggestions[] entry, and every reviewer prompt states the 0.7 confidence ladder that decides blocking vs note. A reviewer reasoning in those terms, with the field already in its output contract one array over, attaches it to the finding itself. Admitted on both arrays rather than forbidden, because the number is real signal a reader wants and rejecting the artifact loses every other finding with it.

id.description: Optional. Present so a fix_suggestions[] entry can reference a note, which fix_suggestions.id already documents as allowed — without this property that reference was unsatisfiable and a reviewer that supplied one failed validation.

decision_ref.description: Same meaning as on a blocking issue. Present here for the same reason `id` is: the invariant reviewer is told to cite the decision a finding relates to, and citing one on an observation it deliberately chose NOT to block on is correct behaviour, not a mistake. Without this property that artifact failed `additionalProperties` and the whole reviewer died — losing every finding it had, including any blockers, over a note it was right to write.

category.description: Same meaning as on a blocking issue. Third instance of the same class after `id` and `decision_ref`: blocking_issues and non_blocking_notes describe the same findings at different confidence, so every descriptive field on a blocker eventually shows up on a note, and each one killed a reviewer via `additionalProperties` before being admitted here. `severity` and `source` are admitted below pre-emptively to close the class instead of losing one more reviewer per field. That pre-emption missed `confidence`, which then killed the `test` reviewer twice on PR #75 — the lesson being that "admit the fields a blocker has" was the wrong frame: the leak-prone set is every field named anywhere in a reviewer's output contract or prompt, and `confidence` was required on `fix_suggestions[]` and cited in all four prompts' confidence ladders.

severity.description: Deliberately NOT the blocker's critical/high/medium enum: a downgraded finding naturally carries values like "low" or "info", and an enum here would trade the additionalProperties cliff for an enum cliff. Notes are commentary — the judge only consumes blocking_issues — so loose typing costs nothing.

source.description: Same meaning as on a blocking issue; loose-typed for the same reason as `severity` above.

confidence.description: Same meaning as on a blocking issue — see there for why this field was the next one certain to leak. This is the array it actually killed reviewers on (PR #75, twice), because the 0.7 ladder sends a low-confidence finding here, so this is exactly where a reviewer has a number in hand and somewhere to put it. Nullable for the same reason as `severity` above.

id.description: Should match the id of a blocking_issues[] or non_blocking_notes[] entry when this suggestion addresses one.

followup_issues.description: Tightly-scoped follow-up issues a human may choose to open. Loose scoping risks an issue/PR loop.
